chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Kurdawayh, who said:
I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a well into which a drop of blood, or intoxicating nabidh, or urine, or wine falls. He said: Thirty buckets are to be drawn from it.

So this report is anomalous and rare, and we have already discussed it earlier, because it includes mention of wine and intoxicating nabidh, which necessitate drawing out all of the water, in addition to the mention of blood. We have already clarified the basis regarding it, and it is possible that, concerning a drop of blood, it may be understood as indicating a type of recommendation, while the reports we cited earlier are understood as indicating obligation, so that the reports do not contradict one another.

key_terms.ثَلَاثُونَ دَلْوًا: the specified amount of water to be removed in this report
key_terms.خَمْرٍ: wine, cited here as a substance causing severe contamination
key_terms.قَطْرَةُ دَمٍ: a small amount of blood falling into the well
key_terms.نَبِيذٍ مُسْكِرٍ: an intoxicating fermented drink mentioned among the contaminants
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is to be drawn out from the well
key_terms.ٱلْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a drop of blood or an intoxicating substance falls into a well according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of a well contaminated by small amounts of impure substances, mentioning a report that prescribes drawing thirty buckets of water. The compiler then notes that this report is anomalous and explains that, to reconcile the narrations, its ruling concerning a drop of blood may be interpreted as recommended rather than obligatory.
